newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Ugandan president commends Asian businessmen.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan president commends Asian businessmen.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, on an official visit to neighbouring Tanzania, has commended the role of Asian businessmen and urged more foreign investment in East Africa.

Speaking at a meeting held in his honour on Saturday by Tanzanian business leaders, he said Asians who were expelled from Uganda by dictator Idi Amin in 1972 were now playing a big role in rebuilding the country.

Amin, who seized power in a coup in 1971, shocked the world when he gave the 70,000 Asians in Uganda -- many of them born there -- three months to leave. Their expulsion was a key factor in the subsequent collapse of the Ugandan economy.
Amin, ousted in 1979, now lives in Jeddah, where he has been granted asylum by Saudi Arabia.

Museveni said he knew that Asian entrepreneurs were often criticised by local Africans. "They argue that they are corrupt and bribe the indigenous people. If people accept bribes they are stupid," he said.
"Frankly, I like them, and if you do not want them here in Tanzania, I'm ready to take them in Uganda."
He said Asian entrepreneurs were prominent in helping Uganda's economic recovery.
Museveni said Uganda believed in the privatisation of enterprises which were unprofitable under state control, and he urged foreign investors to look to East Africa.
"We have plenty of natural resources and stability -- which are important for investors. I think the only problem we had in the past was political confusion," he added.
Museveni paid a one-day visit to Zanzibar on Sunday. He is due to return to Uganda on Monday.
